entries.title: Quantum ingenuity can sidestep limits of conventional chips—while using commercially accessible components
entries.summary: For decades, computers have steadily grown faster and more powerful. Avik Dutt, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Maryland, envisions another dramatic leap forward—one propelled by the quantum properties of light.

entries.title: Laser light reveals where electrons accumulate in atomically thin semiconductor stacks
entries.summary: Stacking semiconductors—the chips that power phones, computers and so much more—enables quicker signal movement with less energy, but how does the process actually work? Turns out shining a literal light on the semiconducting materials can help elucidate how the electrons move…

entries.title: Quantum blueprint maps a practical path to testing unusual entanglement
entries.summary: Adrian Del Maestro knows how to engineer a quantum fingerprint. Rick Mukherjee has a gift for tuning atoms. Their combined expertise has taken a theory sketched out on paper and created a pathway for real experiments. The results, published in the journal Physical Review…
